name: FlowGuard v2
description: Flow-level intrusion detection for modern encrypted traffic.
problem: Signature-based detection misses anything it has not seen, and most published IDS models are benchmarked on traffic that no longer resembles a real network.
architecture: Gradient-boosted trees over 41 flow-level features, with a temporal aggregation window and per-host normalisation.
dataset: CIC-IDS2017 plus a private capture set, deduplicated and rebalanced to avoid the label leakage present in the original splits.

name: PhishSense
description: Classifies phishing emails from headers and body text together.
problem: Body-only classifiers are easy to evade by rewriting copy. Header signals are harder to fake but noisy on their own.
architecture: DistilBERT encoder over the body, concatenated with 18 engineered header features, joined by a small MLP head.
dataset: Public phishing corpora combined with a hand-labelled set of 4,000 messages from a live mailbox.

name: BinSim
description: Finds functions in a stripped binary that match a known vulnerable implementation.
problem: The same vulnerable code gets vendored into dozens of firmware images under different compilers and optimisation levels, and byte-level matching fails immediately.
architecture: Graph neural network over control-flow graphs, trained with a contrastive objective across compiler and optimisation variants of the same source.
dataset: Functions compiled from open-source projects across four compilers and three optimisation levels.

name: Sift
description: Ranks log lines by how unusual they are for that host.
problem: Anomaly detection on logs usually drowns in novelty. Most new lines are new because software changed, not because something happened.
architecture: Per-host template extraction followed by a sequence model over template transitions; scores deviation from that host's own history rather than a global baseline.
dataset: Self-collected syslog from a lab fleet, no labels.
